title: How the gap opens: three costly moves
objectives: Name the three moves that open the behaviour gap.
Explain where a distributor adds the most value.
body_md:
The behaviour gap is the difference between the return a fund delivers and the return its investors actually earn. It opens up because investors: add money after strong performance, when prices are already high; stop SIPs or redeem after falls, missing the recovery; switch funds chasing last year's winner. For many clients, closing this gap matters more to their final outcome than picking the “best” fund. That is where a distributor adds the most value.

> **Investor takeaway:** Your own behaviour can affect your returns as much as the fund you choose.
example: Client adds ₹5 lakh after a 40% year, then stops the SIP after a 15% fall: high prices bought, low prices missed — the gap in action.
say: Closing the gap matters more than picking the best fund for many clients.
A distributor's biggest value is keeping clients on plan.
never: Adding after rallies is the best strategy.
Switching to last year's winner closes the gap.
